ARVO metadata separately reports 2137582c9696b6e38d70b4a0d4199b315c9fd4ce/e53206271db4a83834433ab5f82d16815a18b998 as vulnerable/fixed commits, but the staged patch bundle is commit 3341c7fbfb9bc8e137afd9f16da8cf18eb67b25b (`[fuzzing] Move fuzzing fonts from api/ here`) and does not touch the crashing AAT path. The local HarfBuzz history in the staged repo also contains commit 87205ef935ede70365187549d133014669ea47f2 (`[aat] Make sure Lookup offset is never nulled`), which explicitly fixes testcase 5718889451749376 and matches the reviewed nullable lookup-offset chain, so that commit is recorded as the actual fix here.

bug_description.original: Crash Type: Global-buffer-overflow READ 1 Crash State: BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short AAT::ContextualSubtable::driver_context_t::transition void AAT::StateTableDriver<AAT::ContextualSubtable::EntryData>::drive<AAT::Conte
bug_description.original_source: ARVO-Meta.report.comments[0].content / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / local HarfBuzz history
bug_description.normalized: When the staged font is shaped in the harness's first UTF-8 `hb_shape()` call, HarfBuzz reaches `AAT::ContextualSubtable::driver_context_t::transition()` on a state-table entry whose `currentIndex` action is active. The selected `substitutionTables[currentIndex]` element is a nulled lookup offset that the vulnerable parser accepts because contextual substitution tables use null-enabled `OffsetTo<Lookup<GlyphID>, HBUINT32>` entries and `ContextualSubtable::sanitize()` treats offset 0 as valid. At runtime `subs[currentIndex]` dereferences that slot, `OffsetTo::operator()` returns `Null(Lookup<GlyphID>)`, and the zero-filled null object is dispatched by `Lookup::get_value()` as format 0. `LookupFormat0::get_value()` then returns a non-null `GlyphID *replacement` derived from the null object's `arrayZ` tail using `info[idx].codepoint` as the glyph index. `transition()` checks only that `replacement` is non-null before executing `info[idx].codepoint = *replacement`, and the resulting big-endian `GlyphID` load in `BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short()` reads outside global storage, which AddressSanitizer reports as a global-buffer-overflow.

source.description: First project-side materialization of the attacker-controlled lookup object on the crashing path. The contextual entry's `currentIndex` selects one slot from the font-backed `substitutionTables` list, and this line turns that slot into the `lookup` reference later used to obtain `replacement`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 1680-byte sfnt font whose `morx` contextual subtable reaches the `currentIndex` substitution path during the first `hb_shape()` call at `test/fuzzing/hb-shape-fuzzer.cc:20`. This line reads the selected lookup-offset slot directly from that attacker-controlled font data.
source.note: This is the scored source rather than the harness or earlier state-table plumbing because it is the first project statement that materializes the specific lookup object whose null-offset semantics cause the crash.

sink.description: Final crashing read. Dereferencing the forged `GlyphID *replacement` invokes this big-endian 16-bit load, and ASan reports its first byte as a global-buffer-overflow.
sink.note: The saved ASan report gives `READ of size 1` at `src/hb-machinery.hh:675:13`, with `AAT::ContextualSubtable::driver_context_t::transition` immediately above it on the stack.

root_cause.description: Root cause. Contextual substitution-table entries are stored as null-enabled offsets, so dereferencing a zero `substitutionTables[currentIndex]` slot materializes `Null(Lookup<GlyphID>)` instead of rejecting the malformed font. Later code then treats that zero-filled null object as a real lookup.
root_cause.note: Local commit `87205ef93` fixes testcase `5718889451749376` by changing the contextual substitution list to `UnsizedOffsetListOf<Lookup<GlyphID>, HBUINT32, false>` and by making `Lookup` unusable as a null-pool object (`DEFINE_SIZE_MIN (0)`).

tainted_value_origin.description: The attacker-controlled lookup-offset list enters the accepted `morx` contextual subtable state here. In the vulnerable source this list is `UnsizedOffsetListOf<Lookup<GlyphID>, HBUINT32>` with null-enabled elements, so a zero slot is preserved for later runtime materialization instead of being rejected.
tainted_value_origin.note: Inside `hb-open-type.hh:400-409`, this walks each list element with `OffsetTo::sanitize()`, and `hb-open-type.hh:281-284` returns success immediately when `this->is_null()`, so a nulled lookup offset survives sanitize.

parser_admitted.note: The malformed contextual subtable is admitted because `substitutionTables.sanitize()` accepts the font's lookup-offset list as well-formed even when the selected slot is null.

fixed_text_buffer.note: The ASan stack ends at line 20, so the witnessed crash occurs during the harness's first fixed UTF-8 shaping call on `ABCDEXYZ123@_%&)*$!`.

coarse_trace.summary: The first fixed-string `hb_shape()` call sends the PoC font through HarfBuzz AAT `morx` substitution; the saved ASan stack points to line 20 of this block.

The contextual subtable counts its `currentIndex` and `markIndex` references and sanitizes the `substitutionTables` list, but because each lookup offset is null-enabled the malformed zero slot survives admission.
On the observed `currentIndex` substitution path, `transition()` selects `substitutionTables[currentIndex]` and asks the resulting `Lookup<GlyphID>` for a replacement based on `info[idx].codepoint`.

The selected zero lookup offset materializes `Null(Lookup)`, which `Lookup::get_value()` dispatches as format 0 and turns into a non-null `replacement` pointer computed from the null object instead of from a real lookup table.
Dereferencing `*replacement` performs the final 16-bit big-endian load from that invalid pointer, and ASan reports a global-buffer-overflow read.

fine_trace.note: The saved ASan frame at line 254 is inside this block, so the contextual entry fetched from the font has a live `currentIndex` action on the crashing path. This is the observed control decision that routes execution into the vulnerable current-substitution logic.

This computes the glyph slot whose codepoint becomes `lookup.get_value()`'s `glyph_id`. The staged artifacts prove only that later code uses `info[idx].codepoint`; they do not establish whether `idx` equals the live cursor or a clamp from end-of-text, so this GT makes no stronger claim.

Source. `currentIndex` selects one attacker-controlled slot from the `substitutionTables` offset list and materializes it as `lookup`. The same list previously passed `ContextualSubtable::sanitize()` because `substitutionTables` is declared as `UnsizedOffsetListOf<Lookup<GlyphID>, HBUINT32>` with null-enabled offsets, so a zero slot is accepted and carried to runtime.

The selected list element is a 32-bit offset relative to the beginning of the list itself. On the witnessed chain this element is the malformed lookup offset targeted by the local fix, so this expression forwards that font-supplied offset to `OffsetTo::operator()`.

Root cause. Because the list element type is null-enabled, a zero lookup offset is not rejected here; it becomes `Null(Lookup<GlyphID>)`. In the vulnerable source `Lookup<GlyphID>` still has `min_size == 2`, so the returned null-pool object presents a zeroed `format` field to later lookup dispatch instead of failing closed.
The glyph slot chosen in step 2 supplies `glyph_id = info[idx].codepoint`, and the face provides `num_glyphs`. These become the arguments consumed by the null-derived `lookup` object from steps 3-5.
The zero-filled null lookup from step 5 is interpreted as `u.format == 0`, so dispatch falls into `LookupFormat0` instead of returning null immediately.

On the saved path the later dereference proves this function returned non-null, so the `glyph_id >= num_glyphs` guard did not fire. `replacement` therefore becomes a pointer computed from the zero lookup object's `arrayZ` tail, not from a real sanitized lookup table.
This guard decides whether the invalid pointer reaches the sink. Because frame 1 is line 254 and the crash occurs on `*replacement`, the observed execution took the true branch.
The contextual substitution path dereferences the `GlyphID *replacement` produced by the null lookup and writes the loaded 16-bit value back into the buffer.

Sink. Loading the big-endian `GlyphID` reads from the invalid `replacement` pointer created by steps 3-8. ASan reports the first byte at `src/hb-machinery.hh:675:13` as a global-buffer-overflow 470 bytes past global `indic_table`.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: ARVO metadata's staged `patch.diff` is unrelated commit 3341c7fbfb9bc8e137afd9f16da8cf18eb67b25b, but the staged HarfBuzz repo history also contains commit 87205ef935ede70365187549d133014669ea47f2 (`[aat] Make sure Lookup offset is never nulled`), which changes `UnsizedOffsetListOf`, `ContextualSubtable::substitutionTables`, and `Lookup::min_size` on this exact chain. That source change removes the null-offset admission and null-object materialization path described here.

poc.trigger: Supplying the staged font to `hb-shape-fuzzer` makes the first fixed-string `hb_shape()` call enter a `morx` contextual substitution whose `currentIndex` arm selects a nulled lookup-offset slot. Vulnerable `subs[currentIndex]` materializes `Null(Lookup<GlyphID>)`, `LookupFormat0::get_value()` derives a non-null `replacement` pointer from that zero object, and dereferencing `*replacement` crashes in `BEInt<unsigned short, 2>::operator unsigned short()`.

format.name: sfnt font with morx ContextualSubtable
format.contract: A 1680-byte sfnt font accepted by `hb_face_create()` and exercised through the harness's first UTF-8 `hb_shape(font, buffer, NULL, 0)` call on `ABCDEXYZ123@_%&)*$!`. On the witnessed chain, a `morx` `ContextualSubtable` reaches a state-table entry with `currentIndex != 0xFFFF`, and the selected `substitutionTables[currentIndex]` slot is a null lookup offset (0) that vulnerable `ContextualSubtable::sanitize()` and `OffsetTo` semantics accept. `subs[currentIndex]` therefore materializes `Null(Lookup<GlyphID>)`, `lookup.get_value(info[idx].codepoint, driver->num_glyphs)` dispatches that zero object as `LookupFormat0`, and the returned non-null `replacement` pointer is dereferenced in `transition()`. No broader trigger class beyond this witnessed null-lookup-offset contextual-substitution chain is claimed.
